title: Mapping Schema
description: Validates cross-taxonomy mapping files in governance-commons/mappings/. Mappings record set-theoretic relations between rules in different catalogs. Schema is at stable lifecycle status as of M3 close consolidation 2026-05-30.

x-governance-commons.author: myoung
x-governance-commons.attestation-mechanism: Charter Section 2.4.1 solo-author attestation. Schema-rides-content Path A precedent per Section 10 settled decisions 14, 17, 21, 22: schema lifecycle promoted alongside the 4 mapping files it validates (owasp-llm-to-concerns, owasp-asi-to-concerns, mitre-atlas-to-concerns, stride-to-concerns) at M3 close consolidation 2026-05-30. The 4 stable mappings are the schema's first stable consumers; the schema itself is unchanged in content (schema-version remains 0.1.0), only its lifecycle-status field flipped draft -> stable.
x-governance-commons.ai-assistance: AI drafted based on mappings/README.md and OSCAL mapping model. The 4 M3 Session 2a mappings exercised the schema; promotion to stable at M3 close follows the schema-rides-content Path A precedent established at M1 close (static-analysis-binding schema 0.2.0 -> stable) and reinforced at M2 close (variant 6 attestation-orchestration promotion at 0.3.0 stable). No schema content changed; only lifecycle-status flipped.
x-governance-commons.validation-notes: Schema validated cleanly against 4 mapping files at M3 close (2026-05-30). Future mappings (compliance-to-concerns, framework-to-concerns) inherit this schema; if any future mapping requires a structural extension, the substrate elects between (a) adding optional fields backward-compatibly under schema-version 0.1.x or (b) introducing a new schema-version 0.2.0 with a discriminated additional shape, per the schema-version-management precedent from static-analysis-binding's five-variant evolution.

methodology.description: Free-text description of the mapping methodology used. Per mappings/README.md authoring discipline.

relations.description: The mapping entries. Each entry asserts one relation between a source rule and a target rule.

coverage-gaps.description: Explicit recording of source-side requirements that have no target-side rule addressing them. Per mappings/README.md.

rationale.description: Required per Charter Article II authoring discipline. Why this relation holds.

coverage-dimension.description: Which aspect of the source requirement is covered. Useful when multiple relations partial-cover a single requirement.

gap-description.description: Why no target rule addresses this source requirement

recommended-action.description: Optional. Suggests substrate authoring or consumer-side action to close the gap.
